title: POC Weekly Sync - App Integration (SDK + Tool/Function Calls + Structured Output)
summary: Weekly POC sync reviewing integration progress: SDK usage for function/tool calls, structured output schema results, latency/cost tradeoffs. Decided to run a 1-hour throughput benchmark next week, send pricing for dedicated pilot, and provide updated security pack and sample webhook contract.
topics: Function/tool calling reliability and error handling
Structured output schema mismatches and validation
Security requirements: SSO, KMS, audit logs, data retention
Next steps: benchmark run, pricing, security docs
transcript:
[00:00] Laura Chen: All right everyone, thanks for joining the weekly sync. We have about 55 minutes, so we'll try to run through updates, blockers, and next steps. Miguel and Samir from my side.
[00:12] Priya Nair: Thanks Laura. Quick update from our side — we finished the mobile SDK hookup last night but saw some structured output key mismatches in a couple edge cases.
[00:25] Miguel Torres: Got it. When you say mismatches, is this type coercion or missing fields?
[00:29] Daniel Kim: Mostly missing fields when the model emits slightly different field names, so our JSON schema validation fails in the parser we added. For example, we expected "product_id" but sometimes got "id" or "productId".
[00:42] Samir Patel: That's pretty common — defaults and model drift. We pushed an example handler in the sample SDK that does flexible key mapping and warns instead of failing. Did you pull the latest sample?
[00:54] Daniel Kim: I think we were on the commit before that. We'll pull.
[01:00] Laura Chen: Cool. Also Omar, you were running the structured-output evals against the prompt set? What did you find?
[01:07] Omar Hassan: Yeah, I ran the 500-case validation. Overall pass rate is about 86% with strict schema validation. If we loosen validation to allow aliases and optional fields it's 94%. The failures cluster around product variant descriptions and nested arrays where the model flattens items.
[01:24] Miguel Torres: That aligns with our experience. Two options: 1) tighten the prompt templates to force canonical keys, 2) use the SDK-level post-processor mapping, or 3) add a lightweight canonicalization function server-side. Tradeoffs are complexity vs. correctness.
[01:39] Jess Rivera: From a PM perspective, we prefer not to change product UIs to accommodate model oddities, so we'd rather canonicalize in the backend.
[01:46] Laura Chen: Makes sense. We'll share a sample canonicalizer in the repo today.
[01:52] Hannah Lee: Quick security note — we need confirmation on where logs containing user prompts are stored, and encryption at rest. We also need SOC2 attestation for Redwood's hosted offering if we go that route.
[02:04] Laura Chen: Absolutely. We sent the initial security pack last week; we'll attach the SOC2 report and KMS integration guide again. For hosted, logs are retained per your retention policy and can be routed to your SIEM; for dedicated we can enable customer-managed KMS and audit log forwarding.
[02:20] Hannah Lee: Good. Also SSO — Okta SAML is non-negotiable for our pilot.
[02:25] Samir Patel: We support SAML/Okta for the console — we can set up a test IdP for the pilot. We'll need a contact for the SSO metadata exchange.
[02:34] Hannah Lee: Jess can own that.
[02:36] Jess Rivera: Yep I'll follow up after the call.
[02:40] Laura Chen: Great. Switching to performance: Miguel, you ran the tail-latency tests with the SDK in continuous-batching mode?
[02:47] Miguel Torres: I ran two configs: (A) hosted default batching with max latency target 200ms, (B) aggressive batching for cost savings. For your 512-token average payload, config A gave P95 ~180-220ms depending on network, and config B pushed P95 to 320-380ms but lowered token cost by ~30%.
[03:07] Daniel Kim: For mobile use cases we need under 250ms P95 most of the time. So config A seems safer.
[03:13] Laura Chen: We can tune the batch window smaller — e.g., 10ms instead of 25ms — to reduce tail for mobile requests at the expense of some throughput.
[03:21] Daniel Kim: What's the tradeoff in QPS?
[03:24] Miguel Torres: For your backend, we saw sustained QPS drop about 8–12% because smaller batches reduce GPU utilization. If throughput is low it's fine; if you need peak throughput, consider Dedicated where you can reserve more GPUs.
[03:39] Priya Nair: We're leaning hosted for speed of iteration, but want a dedicated pilot if traffic projections hit the committed tier. We want pricing for both.
[03:48] Laura Chen: We'll send a two-tiered pricing sheet — hosted usage and a 3-month dedicated pilot quote with reserved capacity.
[03:55] Jess Rivera: Could you include burst capacity options? We have promotional spikes.
[03:58] Laura Chen: Yes, we'll include burst policy and SLA info.
[04:02] Omar Hassan: One technical issue: function/tool calling reliability. We've seen occasional 500s from the tool runner when the model calls back to our webhook endpoint via the sample tools layer. Error rates are low but problematic.
[04:16] Miguel Torres: When you say 500s, is that Redwood returning 500 or your tool's endpoint returning 500?
[04:21] Omar Hassan: It's a mix. Sometimes the SDK times out and retries, and the tool runner logs show a schema parse error. Other times the tool responds but the SDK treats it as invalid payload and throws.
[04:33] Samir Patel: Two suggestions: extend the SDK retry/backoff defaults and increase the tool call validation tolerance. We also added an option to stream tool call receipts so you can ACK early and process asynchronously.
[04:45] Daniel Kim: Streaming receipts would help mobile perceived latency a lot.
[04:48] Laura Chen: We have that in 0.9.4 of the SDK sample. I'll paste the release notes in slack after the call.
[04:55] Hannah Lee: On data residency — if we use hosted, can we ensure data for EU customers is kept in eu-1 region?
[05:02] Samir Patel: Yes, region pinning is available. We'll annotate the sample config file.
[05:08] Priya Nair: Back to structured output — could you show an example of the canonicalizer and how it integrates into the SDK pipeline?
[05:15] Miguel Torres: Sure. High-level: the SDK exposes a post-process hook where you can register a canonicalizer function. It runs after model decode but before you persist. We'll share code snippet. If you prefer server-side, we can push a lambda-style example that sits behind your webhook.
[05:29] Daniel Kim: We'll try the SDK hook first.
[05:32] Laura Chen: OK. Next, timeline and benchmarks: we propose a 1-hour throughput run next Tuesday where Redwood will drive X QPS against your staging with representative prompts and you capture P50/P95, error rates, and cost per 1k tokens.
[05:45] Priya Nair: Tuesday works. Can you confirm the exact window and the expected VM/IP allowlist?
[05:49] Laura Chen: We'll send a test plan with IPs and the prompt set. Also we need an account for Okta SAML exchange.
[05:56] Jess Rivera: I'll coordinate with Hannah and share the metadata by EOD Monday.
[05:59] Laura Chen: Great. Any competitors mentioned?
[06:02] Hannah Lee: We looked at ModelServeCo and CloudAI during evaluation, primarily for price comparisons.
[06:07] Miguel Torres: Noted. We'll include a short benchmarking note against general open models — but not competitor messaging.
[06:14] Laura Chen: All right, let's recap action items and owners.
[06:18] Laura Chen: Action items: Laura will send pricing and benchmark plan; Miguel will push sample canonicalizer and SDK hook example; Samir will share SAML test IdP setup instructions and security pack including SOC2 and KMS guide; Jess will provide Okta metadata; Omar and Daniel will pull latest SDK and run a quick validation suite; Priya will confirm Tuesday window.
[06:40] Priya Nair: Sounds good.
[06:42] Laura Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in Slack and put the PRs in the repo.
[06:47] Daniel Kim: One last quick question — is there a recommended monitoring dashboard for structured output regressions?
[06:52] Samir Patel: Yes, Redwood Console has per-route schema drift detection and can alert on regression thresholds; we'll give you access to the demo dashboard.
[06:59] Laura Chen: Okay, that's it. We'll close the call. Thanks all.
